page: Amazon Web Services r6a.large is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng tests, and average for Geekbench single-core and text processing. However, multi-core performance is weak, ranking in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and the bottom 10% for Geekbench multi-core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with small-block cached reads scoring in the bottom 10% and large-block reads and writes in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, the r6a.large is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high parallel compute power. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations both rank in the bottom 10%, indicating that while the memory capacity is high, high-throughput transactional database workloads may face performance bottlenecks. It is suitable for lightweight caching, basic memory-intensive data processing, or general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute resources.
